# Implementation Plan: Queue System (Sprint 5)

**Branch**: `005-queue-system` | **Date**: 2026-03-14 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/005-queue-system/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Implement Sprint 5 queue operations end-to-end on Flutter + Firebase: generate daily queue entries from today's `booked` appointments, power admin queue actions (`next`, `skip`, `no-show`, `rejoin-to-end`), expose customer queue status with privacy-safe visibility, and recalculate wait times as the sum of durations ahead. The implementation reuses the existing feature-first Clean Architecture structure (`admin/queue_management`, `customer/booking`, `customer/entry`, `shared_domain`) and extends the current Firestore-backed repository pattern with atomic/idempotent queue transitions.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.9.0+ / Flutter 3.9.0+  
**Primary Dependencies**: `flutter_bloc` (Cubit), `injectable` + `get_it`, `go_router`, Firebase (`cloud_firestore`, `firebase_auth`, `firebase_crashlytics`), `equatable`, `talker_flutter`  
**Storage**: Cloud Firestore (`organizations/{orgId}/appointments/{id}`, `organizations/{orgId}/queues/{yyyy-MM-dd}`)  
**Testing**: `flutter test`, `bloc_test`, `mocktail` (unit coverage mandatory before merge; no TDD requirement)  
**Target Platform**: Flutter mobile (Android/iOS)  
**Project Type**: Mobile app (feature-first Clean Architecture)  
**Performance Goals**: Queue updates visible to customers within 2s for 95% of state changes; queue actions complete in <2s; 60fps UI interactions  
**Constraints**: Domain layer remains framework-agnostic; single admin per organization scope; atomic + idempotent queue action handling; customer view must not reveal other customer identities  
**Scale/Scope**: Up to 100 same-day appointments per org queue; 1 admin action stream per org; 2 presentation flows (admin queue management + customer queue status)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| **I. Code Quality / Clean Architecture** | ✅ PASS | Queue business rules are planned as domain use cases. Data layer handles Firestore I/O and model mapping only. Presentation uses Cubits only. |
| **II. Flexibility & Extensibility** | ✅ PASS | Implementation targets existing feature modules and shared entities. No cross-feature boundary violations planned. |
| **III. Testing Standards** | ✅ PASS | Plan includes unit tests for queue use cases/repositories and cubit state transitions before PR merge. |
| **IV. UX Consistency** | ✅ PASS | Reuse existing app theme/components, explicit loading/error/empty states, and privacy-safe customer view. |
| **V. Fast Delivery** | ✅ PASS | Delivery focuses only Sprint 5 scope (queue generation, admin actions, customer status, wait estimate). Notifications remain deferred. |
| **VI. Performance Requirements** | ✅ PASS | Firestore query/index strategy and lightweight in-memory wait-time calculation support real-time requirements. |

**Structure Decision**: Reuse and extend the existing `admin/queue_management` scaffold for admin operations, keep customer queue visibility under `customer/entry` (where customer home already lives), and reuse `customer/booking` appointment repository abstractions. This minimizes surface-area changes while maintaining strict clean architecture boundaries.
